turnover_financial.text: main objective of the project is to collect evidence on WTR practices implemented by companies in the European Union, whilst also presenting a comprehensive overview of initiatives undertaken by governments and social partners aimed at altering the organisation and duration of working time. Additionally, the project will assess the benefits and the disadvantages that can arise from WTR both at an individual and firm level. Specifically, the project will investigate impacts on workers’ health and well -being, work-life balance, wages, working conditions, skills development and on firms’ revenues, costs, productivity, work organisation, turnover, training and recruitment practices, experiences of labour shortages and on workforce composition. The contribution resulting from this tender will add to a wider range of deliverables investigating WTR from different angles. The research programme under the SLA encompasses five interconnected research activities: I. An extended systematic literature review and policy update covering all EU -27 Member States, synthesising recent evidence on individual and organisational outcomes of working time reduction, with a particular focus on productivity effects and EU-relevant sources; II. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). Afte r 1973, the decline in working hours slowed and became more varied across countries, with minimal reductions in the European Foundation for the Improvement of Living and Working Conditions 240105/7807 Procurement documents – Part B: Tender Specifications Page 12 of 40 average working week. Background information Over the last 150 years, Europe has witnessed a gradual decline in the number of working hours. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). sla_onsite.text: Jei Tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas, turi apie tai nurodyti pasiūlyme, nurodant teisinį pagrindą. Tiekėjas turi įvertinti ar sutarties vykdymo metu netaps PVM mokėtoju. Jei Tiekėjas vykdydamas sutartį taps PVM mokėtoju, pasiūlyme turi nurodyti kainą su PVM. Pasiūlymų kainos bus vertinamos ir lyginamos su visais mokesčiais, įskaitant PVM. Tuo atveju, kai mokesčius reguliuojančių įstatymų ir jų įgyvendinamųjų teisės aktų nustatyta tvarka perkančioji organizacija pati turi sumokėti PVM į valstybės biudžetą už įsigytą pirkimo objektą, šis mokestis įskaičiuojamas į pasiūlymo kainą (jeigu Tiekėjas jo neįskaičiavo pateikiant pasiūlymą, palyginimo tikslais įskaičiuoja pati perkančioji organizacija). Į pasiūlymo kainą privalo būti įskaičiuoti visi mokesčiai bei visos kitos Tiekėjo patirtos ir (ar) galimos patirti tiesioginės ir netiesioginės išlaidos ir mokesčiai, susiję su pirkimo objekto tiekimu, įskaitant, bet neapsiribojant (išskyrus tuos atvejus, kai pirkimo dokumentuose aiškiai nurodyta, kad tam tikros konkrečios išlaidos neturi būti įskaičiuotos į Sutarties kainą) elektroninių sąskaitų teikimo išlaidos. Pasiūlyme nurodyta kaina ar kainos (įskaitant visus tarpinius skaičiavimus) turi būti nurodomos dviejų skaičių po kablelio tikslumu. Jei trečias skaičius po kablelio yra nuo 0 iki 4, an

turnover_financial.text: main objective of the project is to collect evidence on WTR practices implemented by companies in the European Union, whilst also presenting a comprehensive overview of initiatives undertaken by governments and social partners aimed at altering the organisation and duration of working time. Additionally, the project will assess the benefits and the disadvantages that can arise from WTR both at an individual and firm level. Specifically, the project will investigate impacts on workers’ health and well -being, work-life balance, wages, working conditions, skills development and on firms’ revenues, costs, productivity, work organisation, turnover, training and recruitment practices, experiences of labour shortages and on workforce composition. The contribution resulting from this tender will add to a wider range of deliverables investigating WTR from different angles. The research programme under the SLA encompasses five interconnected research activities: I. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). Afte r 1973, the decline in working hours slowed and became more varied across countries, with minimal reductions in the European Foundation for the Improvement of Living and Working Conditions 240105/7807 Procurement documents – Part B: Tender Specifications Page 12 of 40 average working week. Any reductions in working time at national level since the mid -1990s were largely driven by shifts in labour force participation and the rise in part -time work, resulting from more women entering the labour market. Background information Over the last 150 years, Europe has witnessed a gradual decline in the number of working hours. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023).
